items.answer: Every requirement has concrete input -> WL examples. Indicator 2: no delay -> 0, <=3 days -> 0, >3 days -> 2, >60 days -> 3, >90 days -> 4. Indicator 3: 0 -> 0, 1 -> 1, >1 -> 2. Invalid input throws RangeError.

items.answer: One apparent mismatch: the POC table writes the Indicator 2 option as "≤3 days", while C1 gives the exact string "<=3 days". C1 is the business-confirmed clarification, so the ASCII string "<=3 days" is the only valid one and "≤3 days" throws RangeError. No other contradictions: C1 and C5 agree on trimming and exact matching, and C2 fills the WL values the table leaves out.
items.quote: Indicator 2: "no delay", "<=3 days", ">3 days", ">60 days", ">90 days"

items.answer: Both requirements have the same priority (Must) and are independent, so they can be built and shipped in parallel by two backend developers. No MoSCoW split is needed.

items.answer: daysWithDelayWl(option: string) -> 0|2|3|4 and DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS (5 strings, in order) in src/indicators/daysWithDelay.mjs. delayCountWl(option: string) -> 0|1|2 and DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS (3 strings, in order) in src/indicators/delayCount.mjs. Input is trimmed with String.prototype.trim() and matched exactly and case-sensitively. A non-string (null, undefined, number) throws RangeError. There is no empty-value default: an empty or whitespace-only string is not in the list, so it throws RangeError.
items.quote: `export function daysWithDelayWl(option)` → 0 | 2 | 3 | 4

items.answer: Any value that is not an exact option after trim() throws a RangeError, and so does any non-string. Examples: ">3 Days" (case), ">3  days" (inner whitespace), "≤3 days", "", null, 3. The error message text is not specified (see X-error-message).
items.quote: a non-string input is a RangeError too.

items.question: What should the RangeError message say? C1 and C5 fix the error type only, not the message.
options: Free-form but informative, naming the indicator and the rejected value, e.g. Indicator 2: unsupported option ">3 Days"
A fixed string agreed with the business
items.impact: Neither option changes the mapping or the thrown type. Tests must assert only instanceof RangeError (not the message), so devs and QA stay consistent. If a consumer later parses the message, that would become a contract.

history.question: What should the RangeError message say? C1 and C5 fix the error type only, not the message.

items.answer: RangeError message names the indicator, the rejected value (JSON.stringify of strings; typeof for non-strings) and the allowed options, e.g. 'Indicator 2 (days with delay): invalid option ">3 Days"; expected one of: "no delay", "<=3 days", ">3 days", ">60 days", ">90 days"'. Tests assert the error type (RangeError) and that the message contains the rejected value — never the full text.
items.source: pm: michael 2026-10-06 — C1/C5 fix only the error type; a message that names value and allowed options helps the POC screens and debugging without coupling tests to exact wording.

items.question: Should the exported *_OPTIONS arrays be frozen (Object.freeze) or plain arrays?
options: Frozen: a consumer cannot corrupt the shared option list
Plain arrays: simpler, the contract only says "export const"
items.impact: An internal-safety detail only. Reading the arrays, their order and their contents are the same either way. Tests may assert order and content, not frozenness.

history.question: Should the exported *_OPTIONS arrays be frozen (Object.freeze) or plain arrays?

items.answer: DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS and DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS are exported frozen (Object.freeze) arrays.
items.source: pm: michael 2026-10-06 — They are the single source for the dropdowns rendered by other parts (C4); freezing prevents a consumer from mutating the shared list and breaking the mapping, at no cost to reading or rendering.
